# GitLab Duo CLI (beta) reference

## `duox`

GitLab Duo for your command line.

For detailed feature documentation, see [GitLab Duo CLI](https://docs.gitlab.com/user/gitlab_duo_cli/).

> **Note:** If you use the GitLab Duo CLI through the GitLab CLI (`glab`), replace `duo` with `glab duo cli` in all examples in this reference.

### Synopsis

GitLab Duo CLI ships an interactive terminal UI (TUI) plus auxiliary subcommands for headless workflow runs, configuration, and log management.

### Global options

| Flag                                 | Environment variable                  | Default                     | Values                              | Description                                                                                                                                 |
| ------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------- | --------------------------- | ----------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `-C, --cwd <path>`                   |                                       | _current working directory_ |                                     | Change the working directory.                                                                                                               |
| `--gitlab-base-url <url>`            | `GITLAB_URL`                          |                             |                                     | The URL of the GitLab instance to connect to.                                                                                               |
| `--gitlab-auth-token <token>`        | `GITLAB_TOKEN`                        |                             |                                     | Personal Access Token (PAT) with `api` scope.                                                                                               |
| `--log-level <level>`                | `LOG_LEVEL`                           | `debug`                     | `debug`, `info`, `warning`, `error` | Set the logging level.                                                                                                                      |

| `--enable-project-hooks`             | `GITLAB_ENABLE_PROJECT_HOOKS`         | `false`                     |                                     | Enable loading hooks from the project-level configuration. Disabled by default to prevent running arbitrary code from checked-out projects. |

### `duox` (interactive terminal UI)

Launch the interactive TUI.

#### Synopsis

Running `duo` with no subcommand launches the interactive TUI against the GitLab backend. Use `duo run` for non-interactive / headless execution.

#### Examples

```console
# Start an interactive chat session
duo

# Start a session connected to a specific GitLab instance
duo --gitlab-base-url https://gitlab.example.com --gitlab-auth-token glpat-xxxx

# Start a session using a specific model
duo --model claude_sonnet_4_6
```

#### `tui` options

| Flag                                | Environment variable         | Default     | Values              | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| ----------------------------------- | ---------------------------- | ----------- | ------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `--existing-session-id <sessionId>` | `DUO_WORKFLOW_WORKFLOW_ID`   |             |                     | ID of an existing session to resume.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| `--auto`                            | `DUO_AUTO_APPROVE`           |             |                     | Start in auto mode: tool calls are approved automatically for this session. Toggle at runtime with the `/auto` slash command.                                                                                                                                              |
| `--connection-type <type>`          | `GITLAB_DUO_CONNECTION_TYPE` | `websocket` | `grpc`, `websocket` | (DEPRECATED) Workflow connection type; ignored.                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| `--model <gitlab_identifier>`       | `GITLAB_DUO_MODEL`           |             |                     | GitLab model identifier to use (for example, `claude_sonnet_4_6` or `claude_haiku_4_5_20251001`). Use the `gitlab_identifier` field from <https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/modelops/applied-ml/code-suggestions/ai-assist/-/blob/HEAD/ai_gateway/model_selection/models.yml.> |

### `duox run`

Run a workflow in non-interactive / headless mode.

#### Synopsis

Requires `--goal` (or `DUO_WORKFLOW_GOAL`). Use `--existing-session-id` to resume a previous session. When resuming at a plan approval checkpoint, pass `--approval true|false|once` and optionally `--rejection-reason` to explain a rejection. `--flow-config` accepts either a YAML/JSON file path or inline YAML/JSON content.

#### Examples

```console
# Run a one-shot workflow
duo run --goal "Fix the failing tests in the auth module"

# Run a workflow using a specific model
duo run --goal "Refactor the payment service" --model claude_sonnet_4_6

# Resume an existing session
duo run --goal "Continue" --existing-session-id abc-123

# Resume and approve the proposed plan
duo run --goal "Continue" --existing-session-id abc-123 --approval true

# Resume and reject the plan with feedback
duo run --goal "Continue" --existing-session-id abc-123 --approval false --rejection-reason "Too many files changed at once"

# Run with a flow config file
duo run --goal "Run the developer workflow" --flow-config ./my-flow.yaml

# Run with inline flow config
duo run --goal "Run the developer workflow" --flow-config '{"flowConfigId": "developer"}'
```

#### Required options

| Flag                | Environment variable | Description                     |
| ------------------- | -------------------- | ------------------------------- |
| `-g, --goal <goal>` | `DUO_WORKFLOW_GOAL`  | Goal or prompt for the session. |

#### `run` options

| Flag                                           | Environment variable                      | Default     | Values                  | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| ---------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------- | ----------- | ----------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `--approval <decision>`                        | `DUO_WORKFLOW_APPROVAL`                   |             | `true`, `false`, `once` | Human decision for a plan approval checkpoint. Use alongside `--goal` when resuming a session.                                                                                                                                                                             |
| `--rejection-reason <text>`                    | `DUO_WORKFLOW_REJECTION_REASON`           |             |                         | Free-text feedback explaining why the plan was rejected.                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| `--ai-context-items <contextItems>`            | `DUO_WORKFLOW_ADDITIONAL_CONTEXT_CONTENT` |             |                         | Additional context items as a JSON-encoded array.                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| `--output-format <format>`                     | `DUO_WORKFLOW_OUTPUT_FORMAT`              |             | `text`, `json`          | Output format for the run. `json` emits a single JSON document to stdout and routes logs to stderr; `text` (default) preserves the current human-readable behavior.                                                                                                        |
| `--existing-session-id <sessionId>`            | `DUO_WORKFLOW_WORKFLOW_ID`                |             |                         | ID of an existing session to resume.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| `--connection-type <type>`                     | `GITLAB_DUO_CONNECTION_TYPE`              | `websocket` | `grpc`, `websocket`     | (DEPRECATED) Workflow connection type; ignored.                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| `--model <gitlab_identifier>`                  | `GITLAB_DUO_MODEL`                        |             |                         | GitLab model identifier to use (for example, `claude_sonnet_4_6` or `claude_haiku_4_5_20251001`). ### `duox log`

Log management commands.

#### Subcommands

- [`duox log last`](#duox-log-last)
- [`duox log list`](#duox-log-list)
- [`duox log tail [args...]`](#duox-log-tail-args)
- [`duox log clear`](#duox-log-clear)

#### `duox log last`

Open the last log file in `$EDITOR`.

##### Examples

```console
duox log last
```

#### `duox log list`

Print the paths of all log files.

##### Examples

```console
duox log list
```

#### `duox log tail [args...]`

Tail the last log file.

##### Synopsis

Extra arguments are forwarded verbatim to the platform `tail` command (or PowerShell `Get-Content` on Windows). The log file path is appended automatically.

##### Examples

```console
# Follow the last log file
duo log tail -f

# Show the last 50 lines
duo log tail -n 50
```

#### `duox log clear`

Remove all existing log files.

##### Examples

```console
duox log clear
```
